question.problem: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m\times p$ and $p\times n$ matrices, respectively. What is the image of $\text{Col}({B}^{T}\,{A}^{T})$ under the action of $AB?$
question.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $AB$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $AB:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ (ab)_{1} & (ab)_{2} & ⋯ & (ab)_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{AB}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $AB$ must be $\text{Col}(AB),$ the column space of $AB.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(AB)$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}((AB)^{T})=\text{Col}({B}^{T}\,{A}^{T})$ must be $\text{Col}(AB).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.
